Where condo stock concentrates: this page names no buildings and no concentration — it is a plans page.

The OCP structure a parcel can sit under: Introduction; Land Use; Policy; Implementation; Maps; Glossary & Amendments; Schedule A — Regional Context Statement; Schedule B — Neighbourhood Plans; Schedule C — Mountain View Heritage Conservation Area; Schedule D — Development Permit Areas.

Schedule B neighbourhood plans, as listed on the City's page: B1 Agricultural Area Plan; B2 Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan; B3 Downtown Neighbourhood Plan; B4 Eastern Hillsides Neighbourhood Plan; B5 Sardis Neighbourhood Plan; B6 South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan; B7 Yarrow Neighbourhood Plan.

items.t: The plan stack, as verified: the Official Community Plan is Bylaw 2025, No. 5500 — "Chilliwack 2050" — presenting a long-term vision and growth strategy covering land use/transportation/utility, economic development, environmental protection/enhancement and social/cultural initiatives, with growth strategies for residential (urban, rural and hillside), commercial, industrial and institutional uses and protection of the Agricultural Land Reserve.

Neighbourhood-plan citations, corrected: the Sardis Neighbourhood Plan is Schedule B5 of Bylaw 5500 (not "Schedule D / Bylaw No. 5024" — no source opened confirms what Bylaw 5024 was); the Agricultural Area Plan is Schedule B1; the Eastern Hillsides Neighbourhood Plan is Schedule B4.

ALR frame: What is established: inside the ALR, one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m² (no more than 1,000 m² of fill), a secondary suite only within the principal residence, and at most one additional residence of up to 90 m² (parcels 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (parcels over 40 ha); subdivision and non-farm use inside the ALR require Agricultural Land Commission approval; and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)) — which is why no ALR parcel is condo stock.

blocks.text: Good to know about Chilliwack Land Use Plans

items.t: This page is a planning page wearing a real-estate address.

The page's schedule labels belong to the previous OCP. Sardis is Schedule B5 of Bylaw 5500 and the Agricultural Plan is Schedule B1; Eastern Hillsides is B4; Schedule C is a heritage conservation area and Schedule D is the permit-area schedule. Do not copy the page's "Schedule D / Bylaw No. 5024" Sardis citation into an offer or a listing.
One of the page's named plan areas is not in the city at all.

The hillside rules are two permit areas, not one. Schedule D lists D-2 Hillside Environment and D-5 Hillside Development separately; the page's single "DPA2 Hillside & Upland" conflates them, and which one applies changes what a hillside parcel must produce before it can be built on.

The 67% ALR figure is page copy, not a verified share. No City or ALC source opened states it; what is verified is the legal frame the boundary protects (ALC approval for subdivision/non-farm use; the 500 m² / suite-inside / 90 m² / 186 m² residence frame; the stratification bar).
The floodplain bylaw number on the page could not be confirmed.
Read B5 before marketing Sardis infill potential on it.

Chilliwack's statistics gap is structural, not an oversight. SnapStats covers 14 communities and Chilliwack is not one of them; CADREB publishes board-wide statistics only. Any Chilliwack "median" quoted from a Fraser Valley source is a different board's number attached to the wrong city.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Chilliwack Land Use Plans

items.t: Development Permit Areas: the City's Schedule D separates D-2 Hillside Environment from D-5 Hillside Development — confirm which areas apply to the parcel and what reports they require before pricing a subdivision or a build.

Subdivision / servicing process — number held not confirmed: The candidate "Land Development Bylaw 2014, No. 3055" is not adopted as the servicing citation here; the documented process is the City's subdivision route through the Approving Officer and the Preliminary Layout Assessment (PLA) process, with servicing requirements confirmed with the City per parcel.

ALR block (ALR ground exists in Chilliwack — Schedule B1 is the Agricultural Area Plan): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m² (no more than 1,000 m² of fill), suite within the principal residence only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

blocks.text: Good to know about Chilliwack Land Use Plans

items.t: Do not copy the page's labels into an offer or a listing.

"DPA2" does not exist as the page names it: the City's Schedule D carries D-2 Hillside Environment and D-5 Hillside Development as separate areas — a hillside parcel can sit under either or both, with different diligence attached, and the page's single "DPA2 Hillside & Upland" label hides that split.

Rosedale is not a City of Chilliwack plan area at all: it has no plan in Schedule B and sits in FVRD Electoral Area D — a City plans page carrying a Rosedale village plan is describing another jurisdiction's ground.
